title: 让 (ràng) in Chinese: HSK 2 Grammar with Examples
description: How to use 让 (ràng) to ask, let or make someone do something: the word order, 让我看看, feelings, 不让 and 没有让, common mistakes and HSK 2 examples.
h1: How to Use 让 (ràng): Making or Letting Someone Do Something
lede: 让 (ràng) is the everyday word for getting someone else to do something. Depending on the context it means ask, tell, let or make, and it always comes before the person, with the action after them.

paras: A is the person (or thing) behind the action, B is the person who does it. The person comes straight after 让, and the action comes after the person. When the speaker is a teacher, a doctor or a parent, 让 usually means tell or ask someone to do something.

examples.py: Lǎoshī ràng wǒ dú zhè běn shū.
examples.en: The teacher asked me to read this book.
The doctor told him to get plenty of rest.

examples.py: Péngyou ràng wǒ bāng tā zhǎo gōngzuò.
examples.en: My friend asked me to help him find a job.

examples.zh: 我让他明天给我打电话。
examples.py: Wǒ ràng tā míngtiān gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.en: I asked him to call me tomorrow.

paras: 让 also means let or allow. Without a subject, 让 + person + verb is a request or an offer: 让我看看 is the normal way to say let me have a look, and 让我来吧 offers to do something for someone.

After the person, 让 can be followed by an adjective or a feeling instead of an action. Then it means make: something makes someone happy, tired or not want to do something. The first part is often a thing or an event, not a person.

examples.py: Zhè jiàn shì ràng wǒ hěn gāoxìng.

examples.zh: 这么冷的天气让我不想出门。
examples.py: Zhème lěng de tiānqì ràng wǒ bù xiǎng chūmén.
examples.en: Cold weather like this makes me want to stay in.

paras: To say someone won't let you do something, put 不 before 让: 不让. For the past, use 没有让. If someone told you not to do something, the negative goes after the person instead, with 不要 or 别: 老师让我们不要说话 means the teacher told us not to talk.
For a question, add 吗 at the end, or use 让不让.

examples.py: Bàba bú ràng wǒ kàn diànshì.
examples.en: Dad won't let me watch TV.
The teacher told us not to talk.

examples.py: Nǐ māma ràng nǐ qù ma?
examples.en: Is your mum letting you go?

examples.py: Nǐ māma ràng bu ràng nǐ qù?
examples.en: Is your mum going to let you go or not?

paras: The most common mistake is to translate make with 做. 做 means to do or make a thing, such as food or homework. To make someone feel or do something, use 让: 他让我很高兴, not 他做我很高兴.
Also, 了 does not go straight after 让. Put it after the second verb or at the end of the sentence.

examples.zh: 他让我们等了一个小时。
examples.py: Tā ràng wǒmen děng le yí ge xiǎoshí.
examples.en: He kept us waiting for an hour.

worksheet.title: 让 (ràng) Worksheet: HSK 2 Printable with Answers
worksheet.description: A free printable 让 (ràng) worksheet for HSK 2: 20 exercises (choose 让, 不让 or 没有让, word order, fix the mistake) with an answer key.

exercises.h2: Choose 让, 不让 or 没有让
exercises.instructions: Write 让, 不让 or 没有让 in each gap. The English tells you what the sentence means.

items.en: The doctor told him to drink plenty of water.
Dad doesn't let me go out on my own.
Yesterday Mum didn't ask me to go and buy food.
This made me very unhappy.
Mum doesn't let me drink coffee in the evening.
Let me think.
He didn't ask me to tell you about this.

items.zh: 天气太冷了，妈妈＿＿孩子出去玩。
items.en: It's too cold, so Mum won't let the children go out to play.
I asked him to come to my place tomorrow.

exercises.instructions: Write the words as one correct sentence with 让.

items.en: The teacher asked me to read this book.
Dad doesn't let me watch TV.
Exams make me really tired.
Let him come in.
Mum didn't let me go.
The teacher told us not to talk.

exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Write the correct sentence.

items.en: He made me very happy.

items.zh: 他让了我们等一个小时。
items.en: He kept us waiting for an hour.
answers: 他让我们等了一个小时。

items.en: Dad doesn't let me watch TV.
The doctor told him to get plenty of rest.
My mum won't let me go.
